newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Woodhead sees continued revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Woodhead sees continued revenue growth.

text.p: Woodhead Industries Inc expects continued revenue growth in the second quarter, as it expands its niche manufacturing products business, its chief executive officer said Friday.
"I would suspect that our second quarter is going to be in the range of about $35 million in revenues," C. Mark DeWinter, Woodhead's president and chief executive told Reuters.
Woodhead, a maker of electrical connectors and other safety-related products, reported revenues for its fiscal second quarter ended March 30, 1996 of $31.7 million.
The company had revenues of $123.7 million and profits of $10.7 million for its fiscal year ended September 28, 1996, up from $120.0 million and $9.2 million in 1995.
In its fiscal 1997 first quarter ended December 28, 1996, Woodhead had sales of $32.2 million and net income of $2.6 million, or $0.24 a share.

The company said it was comfortable with consensus estimates of earnings of $3.1 million, or $0.28 a share, in the second quarter of 1997, up from $2.6 million or $0.24 reported in the same period a year ago.

DeWinter said Woodhead's future growth will focus on three areas: development of new products, expansion into unserved geographical markets and focused acquisitions that give Woodhed either new products or new technologies.
DeWinter said the 75-year-old company was built around the concept of addressing unique customer problems that are not otherwise covered by available products.
"The two principal economic drivers in our business are plant investment in industrial machinery and equipment and the level of factory utilization capacity," he said.
DeWinter said the company plans to spend $15 million in 1997 investing in plant expansions in Mexico, the United Kingdom and Germany.
"We're now at a point where we need additional floor space capacity on a global basis," he said.
DeWinter added it is not easy to find companies to acquire that make a strategic fit for a niche manufacturer.
"Because we're very much of a niche company, it's very difficult to find companies exactly like us and approach them on a possible acquisition," he said.
"We're always looking for expansions that would give us either additional products or some needed channels," he said.
Woodhead shares were trading off 5/8 at 15-1/2.
